narrative: The model predicted a 68.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that estimate was high enough to trigger denial, your law school application was rejected. The strongest factor was your third-year class decile: you are in decile 1, while accepted students average about 5.79. That very low relative academic standing was the main reason the prediction leaned toward failure. Your LSAT score of 41 was above the accepted-student average of about 37, so it actually pushed toward passing; however, it was only the second-most influential factor and was not enough to outweigh the academic-standing concerns. Your first-year class decile was also low—2 compared with an accepted average of 6.00—and it further pushed the prediction toward failure. Next, speak with admissions or an academic advisor about what evidence could strengthen a future application. Ask how to improve your class standing in advanced coursework, whether a delayed reapplication or additional academic program would help, and whether you can provide context for the low deciles. You should also ask whether updated grades, a supplemental statement, or documented circumstances could be considered if you reapply.
